title: SQL Query Builder
description: Build a SQL query builder with method chaining, parameterized queries, joins, subqueries, and aggregation.

steps.title: Create base Query class
steps.description: Build a Query class that supports method chaining: `.select('name', 'age').from('users').where('age > 18')`. Each method returns `this` for chaining. Implement a `.build()` method that generates the SQL string. Print the generated SQL to console.
hints: Store clauses in arrays or strings that reset method builds the final SQL
.where() should handle multiple conditions joined with AND
.build() concatenates clauses: SELECT ... FROM ... WHERE ...

verification.successMessage: Query class generates valid SELECT-FROM-WHERE SQL
verification.failureMessage: Generated SQL is missing expected clauses

steps.title: Add parameterized queries
steps.description: Implement parameterized values using numbered placeholders (`$1`, `$2`) for user-supplied values. The `.where()` method should accept both string conditions and `{ column: value }` objects. `.build()` returns `{ sql: string, params: array }`. Print both SQL and params.
hints: Track a parameter counter that increments with each bound value
Replace values with $N placeholders and push actual values to a params array
For object-style where({ id: 5, status: 'active' }) generate column = $1 AND column2 = $2

verification.successMessage: Parameterized queries generate correct placeholders and params array
verification.failureMessage: Parameter placeholders or params array is missing or incorrect

steps.title: Implement JOIN support
steps.description: Add `.innerJoin(table, condition)`, `.leftJoin(table, condition)`, and `.rightJoin(table, condition)` methods. Each accepts a table name and an ON condition string. Support chaining multiple joins. Print the SQL with JOIN clauses.
hints: Each join type adds a clause like 'INNER JOIN table ON condition'
Store joins in an array and append them between FROM and WHERE in build()
ON conditions can also be parameterized for safety

verification.successMessage: JOIN clauses are generated with correct syntax
verification.failureMessage: JOIN SQL is missing the ON condition or wrong join type

steps.title: Add aggregation and grouping
steps.description: Implement `.groupBy('column')`, `.having('condition')`, and aggregate methods `.count()`, `.sum('col')`, `.avg('col')`. Aggregates should replace selected columns. Print the SQL with GROUP BY and HAVING clauses.
hints: groupBy stores columns and appends GROUP BY col1, col2 in build()
having stores a condition string that goes after GROUP BY
Aggregate functions wrap columns: COUNT(*), SUM(col), AVG(col)

verification.successMessage: Aggregation and grouping SQL is generated correctly
verification.failureMessage: GROUP BY or aggregate functions missing from generated SQL

steps.title: Implement subqueries
steps.description: Allow a Query instance to be used as a subquery inside WHERE clauses (`.where('id IN', subQuery)`) and FROM clauses (`.from(subQuery, 'alias')`). The subquery should be wrapped in parentheses and merged into the parent query's params. Print the nested SQL.
hints: Detect if a value is a Query instance and call build() on it
Wrap subquery SQL in parentheses and merge its params array
For FROM subquery, append an alias: FROM (SELECT ...) AS alias

verification.successMessage: Subqueries are correctly nested in parentheses
verification.failureMessage: Subquery is not wrapped in parentheses or params are not merged

steps.title: Add ORDER BY, LIMIT, OFFSET
steps.description: Implement `.orderBy('column', 'ASC'|'DESC')`, `.limit(n)`, and `.offset(n)` methods. Ordering accepts multiple columns. LIMIT and OFFSET use parameterized values. Print the complete SQL with pagination clauses.
hints: orderBy stores column + direction pairs, appended as ORDER BY col1 ASC, col2 DESC
limit and offset are appended after ORDER BY
Use $N parameters for limit and offset values

verification.successMessage: ORDER BY, LIMIT, and OFFSET clauses are generated correctly
verification.failureMessage: Sorting or pagination clauses missing from generated SQL

steps.title: Build an Insert/Update/Delete builder
steps.description: Add `.insert(table, data)`, `.update(table, data)`, and `.delete(table)` static methods that return Query instances. `.insert()` generates INSERT INTO table (cols) VALUES ($1, $2). `.update()` generates UPDATE table SET col = $1. `.delete()` generates DELETE FROM table. Support `.returning('id')`. Print the final SQL.
hints: insert() extracts keys for column list and values for $N placeholders
update() generates SET col1 = $1, col2 = $2 from the data object
returning('col') appends RETURNING col to INSERT, UPDATE, or DELETE

verification.successMessage: Insert, Update, and Delete builders generate correct SQL
verification.failureMessage: One or more mutation query builders failed to generate valid SQL
